backward_compat_traps.rule: PSI5 carries data as current modulation on a two-wire current loop, NOT as a voltage on a dedicated single signal wire.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating PSI5 like a voltage single-wire interface (e.g. SENT's single signal wire) is wrong — PSI5 modulates the supply current on the shared two-wire loop.

backward_compat_traps.rule: PSI5 data is Manchester-coded (embedded bit clock), not pulse-width nibble timing.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming SENT-style (12 + value ticks) nibble pulse-width timing is wrong for PSI5.

backward_compat_traps.rule: In synchronous mode the ECU sync pulse triggers time-slot transmission; in asynchronous mode there is no sync pulse.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Expecting a sync pulse in asynchronous mode, or expecting autonomous transmission in synchronous mode, breaks timing.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The telegram error check is a 2-bit CRC, a 3-bit CRC, or a parity bit depending on the data word length.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Hard-coding a single error-check width fails for telegram formats that use a different CRC/parity option.

previous_versions: PSI5 evolved from earlier peripheral sensor interface generations; PSI5 is the two-wire current-loop sensor<->ECU interface with current modulation, Manchester coding, synchronous/asynchronous modes, and parallel-bus time slots.

key_changes.summary: Two-wire current-loop automotive sensor interface: loop-powered sensor, current-modulation transmission of Manchester-coded telegrams, synchronous (sync-pulse time slots) and asynchronous modes, point-to-point / parallel-bus / daisy-chain (universal timing) topologies, telegram with 2-bit/3-bit CRC or parity, 125/189 kbps, and the PSI5-P point-to-point variant.

fields.version_naming_history_note: PSI5 (Peripheral Sensor Interface 5) is an automotive sensor interface specification. Facts here are grounded in the PSI5 Technical Specification: a two-wire current loop (power + data on the same wires), current-modulation transmission of Manchester-coded telegrams, synchronous (sync-pulse-triggered time slots) and asynchronous modes, point-to-point / parallel-bus / daisy-chain (universal timing) topologies, a telegram with start condition + data bits + optional region/status + 2-bit/3-bit CRC or parity, bit rates of 125 and 189 kbps, and the PSI5-P point-to-point variant.
